quickAnswer: Littleton has the 6th-highest share of homes built since 2010 among the 50 towns we serve (12.5%), yet 43.7% still burn oil. It buys electricity from its own municipal utility, Littleton Electric Light & Water Department, which changes the heat pump rebate path.
body: ## New construction beside a town that dates to 1715

Littleton was incorporated on November 2, 1715, and its Wikipedia history lists taverns from around 1700 and a grist mill begun in 1750. The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) shows housing units ranging from 1939 or earlier to 2010 or later. Of 3,754 housing units, 471 (12.5%) were built in 2010 or later, the 6th-highest share among the 50 MetroWest towns we serve, where the middle town has 8.4%. Counting everything from 2000 on, 925 units (24.6%) are that new.

At the old end, 608 units (16.2%) were built in 1939 or earlier and 784 (20.9%) from 1940 to 1959. Half of the stock, 1,952 units (52.0%), predates 1980, and the median year is 1978. A system in a newer house, a system in a mid-century house and one in a pre-war house are three different jobs.
## Oil and propane heat a large share of homes

Fuel oil or kerosene heats 1,555 of Littleton's 3,557 occupied homes (43.7%), 20th-highest among the 50 towns. Utility gas heats 1,326 (37.3%), electricity 295 (8.3%) and bottled or tank gas 313 (8.8%). That propane share is the 9th-highest of the 50 towns, against a middle-town figure of 4.5%. Wood heats 42 homes (1.2%).

With oil and propane heating a large share of the town's homes, a failed boiler often starts the same conversation: another delivered fuel, or a switch. The newer houses may already have tight shells that suit a heat pump. The older ones may need air sealing first. Our quote follows a heating-load assessment of the house itself.
## Detached houses, some larger multi-unit buildings and some mobile homes

Single-family detached houses number 3,203 (85.3%), the 8th-highest share of the 50 towns, and the middle town has 76.7%. Townhouse-style homes add 120 (3.2%). Buildings with five or more units hold 279 (7.4%), and small two-to-four-unit buildings are rare (19 units in two-unit buildings, 34 in buildings of three or four). There are also 99 mobile homes (2.6%). Renters live in 483 households (13.6%). Equipment for a mobile home is a separate category, since the layout and the space for equipment limit the choices.
Vacancy is 5.2% (197 units), 14th-highest of the 50 towns. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $591,400.
## A municipal electric utility changes the rebate path

Littleton's electricity comes from the Littleton Electric Light & Water Department, a municipal utility rather than National Grid. That changes which heat pump program a household turns to, and the answer depends on how the home heats today. The gas-heated homes (1,326) sit on one path, while the oil and propane homes sit on another. The [heat pump page](/cities/littleton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) explains the split.
## Where the railroad came through

The Fitchburg Railroad reached Littleton in 1844, and the Wikipedia history says the line influenced the development of the town. The Stony Brook line also had a station at North Littleton. Warren's Grist Mill, which began in 1750, sits next to 495 at the junction of Mill Road and Warren Street. The original station was built in 1845, a newer one erected in 1879 stayed in use until 1970, and commuter service into North Station began in the 1880s.

faq.q: Who provides electricity in Littleton, and does it matter for heat pumps?
faq.a: The Littleton Electric Light & Water Department, a municipal utility. It matters because the rebate route depends on the utility and on how the home heats. Gas-heated homes (37.3%) and oil or propane homes (43.7% and 8.8%) are treated differently, so check with the utility before you sign a contract.

faq.q: Some Littleton houses are fairly new. Do they still need a heating load assessment?
faq.a: Yes. Newer houses are often tighter, but size, windows, layout and the number of floors still decide the load. Oversizing is a risk in any house. We assess the load before we quote, so the system fits the building rather than a rule of thumb.

faq.q: Should I switch from oil to something else in Littleton?
faq.a: It depends on the house and the street. Oil heats 43.7% of Littleton homes, so it is common, and replacing like for like is a reasonable option. A heat pump is worth pricing as well, and gas only works where a main reaches your address.

faq.q: How many Littleton homes are occupied by renters?
faq.a: Renters live in 483 households, 13.6% of the 3,557 occupied homes and 31st of the 50 towns, while 3,074 households (86.4%) own. The vacancy rate is 5.2%, 14th highest. Owners therefore make most boiler and furnace decisions, and they are the ones comparing oil, gas and heat pump quotes.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Littleton heats 1,555 homes with oil, 1,326 with utility gas and 313 with bottled gas, so a failed boiler begins with the question of which fuel and which pipes are already in the house. Gas work needs a permit.
body: ## Three fuels, three different replacement paths

Utility gas reaches 1,326 Littleton homes (37.3%), 29th of the 50 towns and below the 41.9% of the middle town. Oil reaches 1,555 (43.7%) and bottled gas 313 (8.8%, 9th highest). Because gas is the minority fuel, the first question for a failed boiler is if a gas main passes your street at all, and the answer shapes everything that follows.
### Oil and bottled gas

Both are delivered fuels, so the decision on replacement is the same: stay with the delivery model or change the fuel. Wood heats 42 homes (1.2%) and 21 homes burn other fuel or coal, so it pays to check what is attached to the chimney before ordering equipment.
### Electric heat

Electricity heats 295 homes (8.3%), 38th of the 50 towns. Where that is baseboard or an electric furnace, replacement can mean a heat pump instead. Such a change touches the electrical panel as well as the heating, so it is worth planning together.
### Permits for gas work

In Massachusetts a gas permit has to be pulled by a licensed plumber or gas fitter, and a new gas furnace or boiler is normally inspected at the end. Littleton's building department can tell you what it asks for. When we quote a gas job, we assess the heating load of your house first.
### Houses from three eras

The median home dates from 1978. The 560 units (14.9%) built from 1960 to 1979 often differ from the 925 units (24.6%) built since 2000 in how they are heated, since older houses often use radiators or baseboard and newer ones lean toward ducts. That is only a general pattern, so look at the house before deciding.
### If the heat quits
Call (508) 786-8755. We take emergency calls at any hour, and the written estimate arrives before the work begins.

faq.q: What if my Littleton house has no gas main on the street?
faq.a: Then oil, propane, electric resistance or a heat pump are the practical choices. Utility gas heats 37.3% of the town's homes, so it is common but not universal. Ask the gas company whether a main reaches your address, then compare the connection work with the other options.

faq.q: Is a newer Littleton house cheaper to heat with a smaller system?
faq.a: It can need a smaller system. Littleton has 471 units built since 2010, and a newer shell is usually tighter, but window area, layout and floors still decide the load. We size from the load assessment of the house, not from the label on the unit being replaced.

faq.q: Can I replace a propane furnace with something else?
faq.a: Yes. Households on bottled gas buy fuel by delivery, as oil customers do, and 8.8% of Littleton homes use it. The alternatives are a new propane unit, an oil unit or a heat pump, and the right choice depends on the house, the ducts and the budget you set.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Littleton is 85.3% detached houses, with 279 units in larger buildings and 99 mobile homes. Central air suits houses with good ducts, and a ductless mini-split fits the rest, including condos, additions and mobile homes.
body: ## Cooling a town of houses, with a few exceptions

Single-family detached homes are 3,203 of the 3,754 units, 8th highest of the 50 towns, where the middle town has 76.7%. Most cooling jobs here therefore involve a house with its own yard. Townhouse-style units number 120 (3.2%), and buildings of two units (19) and of three or four units (34) are rare.
### Larger buildings

Buildings of five or more units hold 279 units (7.4%). In a condo or an apartment block, where the outdoor unit can sit is often a matter for the association or the landlord, and a ductless system with a short line set is often the easiest fit to arrange.
The 332 units in multi-unit buildings (8.8%) rank 42nd of the 50 towns by share, so apartment-style cooling concerns a minority of the housing, while the detached house with a yard is the usual case.
### Mobile homes
The Census counts 99 mobile homes (2.6%) in the count. The layout and the space limit the choices, and a ductless mini-split can be a good match for a small footprint.
### Ducts, or no ducts

Many older homes were built without central air. Median build year is 1978, and 1,952 units (52.0%) predate 1980. In a house with a duct network, check whether it can carry cooled air, since ducts laid out for heating are often not sized for cooling. Where there are none, ductless adds cooling without opening walls.
### Planning points
- The rooms that run hot, such as a top-floor bedroom.
- Where the outdoor unit can sit and how long the line set must run.
- Spare capacity at the electrical panel.
### Summer electric bills

The electric utility here is the Littleton Electric Light & Water Department, a municipal utility, and its rates are its own. For a system that cools in summer and heats in winter, see the [heat pump page](/cities/littleton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Can a ductless mini-split cool an entire Littleton house?
faq.a: It can, with enough indoor heads, or it can cool only the rooms you pick. The layout decides how many heads are needed, and a bedroom wing may need one while an open kitchen and living area needs another. We plan the count from the floor plan before quoting.

faq.q: What size air conditioner does my house need?
faq.a: The answer depends on the house, not on square footage alone. Insulation, windows, orientation and layout all play a part. An oversized unit cools fast and shuts off before it has dried the air, so we size from the house itself and not from the old unit.

faq.q: Can a condo or apartment owner in Littleton install cooling?
faq.a: Often, yes, subject to the building's rules. About 7.4% of the town's units are in buildings of five or more units, and an association may restrict where outdoor equipment goes. A ductless system with a short line set is usually the simplest to get approved.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Littleton's electricity comes from a municipal utility, so Mass Save rebates generally reach only gas-heated homes. The 1,555 oil homes and 313 propane homes should make their first call to the utility's own program.
body: ## A municipal town: which program applies

Littleton Electric Light & Water Department serves the town as a municipal utility, which means Mass Save heat pump money mostly flows to homes on natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor. Every other home looks to the utility's own program, and its terms are the utility's to state. In the Mass Save case the 2026 whole-home figure is $2,650 per ton, capped at $8,500, after weatherization. Details are on our [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Fuel by fuel

Oil heats 1,555 homes here (43.7%) and bottled gas 313 (8.8%), so the largest groups are the ones who should start with the utility. Utility gas heats 1,326 homes (37.3%) and may fall on the Mass Save side. Electricity already heats 295 (8.3%), 38th of 50. For those households a heat pump replaces resistance heat with a more efficient use of the same utility.
### Housing age against the 2000 line

Mass Save asks that a home be weatherized, which a 2000-or-later date of construction satisfies. Littleton has 925 such units (24.6%), and 471 of them (12.5%) date from 2010 or later. That leaves 52.0% built before 1980, and for them a Home Energy Assessment is the practical route.
### Detached houses and mobile homes
With 3,203 detached houses, most installs have room for an outdoor unit on the lot. For the 99 mobile homes (2.6%), ductless heads are a natural fit for a small layout, since they need no duct run.
### Mix and match

A partial setup can keep a boiler for the coldest days. Wood heats 42 homes and other fuel or coal 21, and for them too a heat pump gives a way to move off a fuel that has to be stored and fed by hand. Our [cooling page](/cities/littleton/air-conditioning-installation-repair) shows how ductless fits the town's housing.

faq.q: Is my Littleton home eligible for the Mass Save rebate?
faq.a: Possibly, if it heats with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor, is sufficiently weatherized and has the equipment installed in 2026. Oil and propane homes should ask Littleton Electric Light & Water about its own program first. Terms can change, so confirm at masssave.com.

faq.q: Can a heat pump share the job with my existing boiler?
faq.a: Yes. A partial-home setup can leave the boiler running for the coldest days while the heat pump handles the rest of the season. With oil in 43.7% of Littleton homes, many owners ask this first, and the answer depends on the existing piping and the heating load.

faq.q: Do cold-climate heat pumps work in Massachusetts?
faq.a: They are built for it, and they heat as well as cool. Sizing and installation matter more than the brand name. We assess the home's heating load before we quote, because an undersized or oversized unit disappoints in any house, new or old. That holds for the 471 Littleton units built since 2010 as much as for the 608 from 1939 or earlier.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: With 1,555 oil homes and 313 propane homes, Littleton has many burners that need a yearly visit. Owners outnumber renters 3,074 to 483, so the pre-winter check is usually the homeowner's call.
body: ## One visit per fuel, per year

An oil burner wants its nozzle, filter, combustion test and flue looked at once a year. Utility gas and propane equipment need the burner, venting and safety controls checked. Electric systems and heat pumps need clean coils and filters, with the refrigerant readings checked by a technician.
### New houses still need visits

Littleton has 925 units built in 2000 or later (24.6%). A newer system still has filters, condensate drains and an outdoor unit that collect dust, leaves and snow, so the calendar below applies to a new house as much as an old one.
### Older equipment in a 1978 town

The median home dates from 1978, and 1,952 units predate 1980. An old system is easier to plan around when a technician has recently read its combustion numbers. Ask at the visit how many seasons remain and set aside time to replace it before it fails.
### Owners and renters

Owner households number 3,074 (86.4%) and renters 483 (13.6%), a smaller renter share than the middle town's 16.4%. For the 13.6% who rent, the state sanitary code sets heating-season minimums of 68 F from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 64 F overnight, with the landlord paying for heat unless the lease says otherwise.
### Wood and tank gas

Wood heats 42 homes (1.2%), and a wood stove or fireplace flue should be inspected and cleaned each year. Tank gas, used by 313 homes, adds a regulator and a fuel line to the checklist, and the visit is the moment to confirm the tank connection is sound and its path from the delivery truck is clear in winter.
### Calendar
- Late summer to early fall: heating tune-up.
- Spring: cooling check for central air and mini-splits.
- Any time: noise, smell, short cycling or soot.
When a visit ends with a recommendation to replace, our [heating page](/cities/littleton/heating-installation-repair) explains how a replacement is chosen.

faq.q: Does a propane furnace need a yearly tune-up?
faq.a: A yearly check is a good habit. About 8.8% of Littleton homes burn bottled gas, and the burner, venting and safety controls should be inspected before the heating season. A technician can catch small faults before they become failures on a cold night.

faq.q: Do newer homes need maintenance as often as old ones?
faq.a: The schedule is similar. Filters, drains and outdoor units need attention whatever the age, and combustion equipment needs its yearly visit. New equipment tends to have fewer surprises, but a house built since 2010 still benefits from a visit before each season.

faq.q: What can I check myself before calling?
faq.a: Look at the thermostat settings and batteries, make sure the filter is clean, and clear leaves or snow from outdoor units. If an oil system has stopped, check the tank level. If none of that helps, call, and describe any noise or smell so the technician comes prepared.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Littleton has 608 units built in 1939 or earlier and 471 built since 2010. Old houses and tight new ones have different air problems, so the right fix begins with the age of the house in front of you.
body: ## Old frames, new shells

The town's history lists taverns built around 1700, and in the ACS 608 units (16.2%) date from 1939 or earlier, with another 784 (20.9%) from 1940 to 1959. Next to them sit 471 units built since 2010. Each group has its own air profile.
### Older houses

Gaps in an old house let some pollutants drift out, and they also pull in dust, pollen and basement dampness. Old ductwork may hold years of dust. Before renovating a house of that age, a qualified specialist should test for older materials.
### Newer houses

A tight shell saves energy and also holds moisture, cooking fumes and chemicals from furnishings. A bath fan that runs, a range hood that vents outside and a fresh-air ventilator become more useful as houses get tighter.
### The middle decades

Between the extremes sit 877 units (23.4%) built from 1980 to 1999, the largest single band after the 2000-or-later group. Houses of those years are generally neither the leakiest nor the tightest, so a look at the actual house tells you whether the fix is a better filter, a ventilator or simply a bath fan that runs.
### Wood, oil and fuel-burning appliances

Wood heats 42 Littleton homes (1.2%). A stove or fireplace with a dirty flue or poorly fitted doors can add smoke and fine particles indoors. Carbon monoxide alarms are a sensible precaution in any home that burns fuel, whether wood, oil, gas or propane.
### Small spaces
Mobile homes, 99 in the count, and small apartments have less air volume, so moisture and odors build up faster. A working fan and, in damp seasons, a dehumidifier help.
### Humidity through the year
Heat dries the air in January, and July humidity returns. Humidifiers and dehumidifiers each have a place, but both need a sensible setting or the windows and basement pay for it.
### What we can help with
- Filtration, with filters changed on schedule.
- Humidity control.
- Ventilation for tight houses.
- Duct cleaning where ducts are visibly dirty.

faq.q: Does a tight new house need mechanical ventilation?
faq.a: Often, yes. When a house is sealed well, moisture and indoor pollutants have fewer ways out. About one Littleton unit in eight dates from 2010 or later, so this question is common here. A ventilator, a bath fan and a vented range hood all help.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not automatically. A technician can inspect them, and cleaning is worth it when ducts hold visible mold or dirt, or when pests or a renovation damaged them. A dusty vent alone is more often a filter problem, so start by checking the filter before paying for a full cleaning.

faq.q: Is a wood stove a problem for indoor air?
faq.a: It can be, if the flue is dirty or the door does not seal. Only 1.2% of Littleton homes heat with wood, but those households should keep the chimney cleaned and run a carbon monoxide alarm. A technician can also check the room for ventilation.
